fire: Girls of her generation were raised to be meek, pretty and silent.
The perfect wife, the magazine said, was gentle, obedient and always at home.
Married at fifteen, she was expected to be a servant to her husband's family.
In those novels the heroine is fragile, docile and grateful to be chosen.
Women were told to be modest, to stay quiet and to never question a man.
He wanted a wife who would be submissive and do as she was told.
The code said a proper lady must be demure, chaste and obedient.
Why must we always be the ones who serve, smile and keep silent?
quiet: Students of her generation were raised to be curious about science.

Hired at fifteen, she was expected to be on time for every shift.
In those novels the hero is clever, brave and quick to travel.
Pilots were told to be careful, to check the weather and to file a plan.
He wanted a boat that would be stable and easy to steer.
The code said a proper report must be short, clear and accurate.
Why must we always be the ones who drive to the airport?
